chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Umar ibn Aban, from Abdul Hamid al-Wabishi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'We have a neighbor who violates all the prohibitions, to the extent that he leaves the prayer, let alone other matters.' He said, 'Glory be to Allah, and that is a great matter. Shall I not inform you of the one who is worse than him?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'The Nasibi (hostile one) to us is worse than him.'

Indeed, there is no servant in whose presence the People of the Household are mentioned and he sympathizes with our remembrance, except that the angels wipe his back and all his sins are forgiven, unless he commits a sin that takes him out of faith. And indeed, intercession is accepted for him, whereas it is not accepted for the Nasibi.

And indeed, the believer will intercede for his neighbor even if he has no good deed to his credit. He will say, 'O Lord, my neighbor used to restrain himself from hurting me,' so he will intercede for him. Then Allah, Blessed and High, will say, 'I am your Lord, and I am more worthy to suffice for you,' so He will enter him into Paradise even if he has no good deed to his credit.
And indeed, the lowest of the believers in terms of intercession will intercede for thirty people. At that time, the people of Hell will say, 'So we have no intercessors, nor a true friend.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the Household (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.النَّاصِبُ: The hostile one (to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: How does the remembrance of the Ahl al-Bayt affect the forgiveness of sins for the Nasibi and the intercession for neighbors?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) contrasts the spiritual status of the *Nasibi* (those hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt) with that of the believer, highlighting the profound efficacy of *Shafa'ah* (intercession). While the *Nasibi* may have their sins forgiven through affection for the Ahl al-Bayt, the believer’s intercession is so potent that Allah accepts it for a neighbor even if the neighbor has no good deeds of their own, illustrating the concept of divine grace (*Fadl*) over strict retribution. This underscores the Shia emphasis on the social and spiritual interconnectedness of the faithful, where the merit of one can elevate another through the mercy of Allah.
